status: EARLY — one operation is modelled (itembank/items + get, the Item bank read). The other 56 documented (endpoint, action) blocks are not built yet; see spec/coverage.md. The PAGING and TRANSPORT behaviour has been verified against Learnosity's public demo Item bank (2026-08-13, learnosity-sdk-nodejs 0.7.0, v2025.2.LTS); everything else is read off the published reference and is presented as documented, not confirmed. A fact verified on the demo bank describes the mechanism, not the caller's own consumer.
summary: Produces developer COOKBOOK RECIPES for the Learnosity Data API — a precise, host-language-neutral procedure for running a server-to-server job against a Learnosity Item bank: signing, the versioned POST-only transport, paging a result set to completion, reading the response envelope, and verifying the job did what was intended. Documentation-only: it covers the published documentation plus the un-written tricks and tips, and never calls a Learnosity API. It emits a recipe to follow, NOT item content and NOT runnable code.
in_scope: How to read Items from an Item bank (itembank/items, action get) — filtering by reference, status, tags, question type, workflow, creator or time window, and shaping the response with include

How to page a result set to completion — the failure this dialect exists to prevent is a truncated read that returns HTTP 200, meta.status true, and a well-formed but silently incomplete record set, where meta.records counts the page rather than the total
How to sign and send a Data API request with the official Learnosity SDK, and how the versioned POST-only transport differs from the front-end APIs
How to read the response envelope — meta.status as an API-level verdict separate from the HTTP status, and meta.code / meta.message on failure
Rate limiting: per-endpoint quotas over a 5-second window, and how that interacts with exhausting a large result set
The verification steps that tell a developer their job is correct AND complete
out_of_scope: Authoring the assessment item CONTENT being read or written (stems, options, answer keys, passages) — that is L0176. This dialect describes the OPERATION that moves content in and out of a bank; it does not compose the content
Embedding and configuring the Author API authoring experience (item/activity editor and browser) — that is L0177

Delivering assessments to learners (Items API) and reading responses/scores/reports (Reports API) — each its own sibling dialect, none built yet. Say no dialect covers it rather than stretching this one

Data API operations not yet modelled — writes (set/update/delete), the async job family, and the sessions and reports endpoints. spec/coverage.md lists the whole surface; an operation absent from the vocabulary is unbuilt, not unsupported, and must not be guessed at

Calling the Learnosity API. This dialect is documentation-only: the caller's own code signs and sends every request with the caller's own consumer key. L0178 holds no credentials and performs no requests
Integrations for any platform other than Learnosity
Emitting runnable host-language code — the recipe is a language-neutral procedure the caller implements in their own stack
